differences.title: 1. CORE TECHNOLOGY
differences.leftDesc: Leverages Rust for a highly performant, memory-safe, and small binary size for the backend logic and system interactions.
differences.rightDesc: Uses Node.js for backend logic, enabling JavaScript/TypeScript across the stack but leading to larger applications.

differences.title: 2. BINARY SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Produces compact executables by only bundling necessary Rust code and assets, avoiding large runtime dependencies.
differences.rightDesc: Includes a full Node.js runtime and Chromium browser, resulting in significantly larger initial download and install sizes.

differences.title: 3. MEMORY USAGE
differences.leftDesc: Rust's memory management and compilation to native code result in lower RAM consumption compared to Node.js and Chromium.
differences.rightDesc: The embedded Chromium browser and Node.js runtime contribute to substantial memory usage, especially with multiple windows.

differences.title: 3. SECURITY
differences.leftDesc: Rust's strong type system and memory safety features inherently reduce common security vulnerabilities found in languages like JavaScript.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on Node.js's security practices; potential vulnerabilities can arise from external npm packages or JavaScript runtime issues.

differences.title: 4. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Rust's compilation to native code and efficient event loop provide performance close to native applications for most tasks.
differences.rightDesc: Offers good performance for UI and typical desktop app tasks, but Node.js and browser overhead can impact CPU-intensive operations.

differences.title: 5. WINDOWING SYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Employs system APIs for window creation and management, potentially offering a more native look and feel.
differences.rightDesc: Renders UI within an embedded Chromium browser instance, providing consistent rendering but deviating from native UI elements.

differences.title: 6. DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCE
differences.leftDesc: Requires knowledge of web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS/TS) and Rust for backend logic, offering a powerful but steeper learning curve.
differences.rightDesc: Leverages familiar web technologies (HTML, CSS, JS/TS) and Node.js, making it accessible for web developers.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM & COMMUNITY
differences.leftDesc: A younger ecosystem with active community growth, leveraging Rust's robust libraries and web frontend flexibility.
differences.rightDesc: Benefits from a massive, mature ecosystem of npm packages and a vast community, with extensive documentation and support.
